meta.title: Scarlet Thread: Advent Path
meta.notes: confidence 'explicit' = a direct textual or narrative connection; read the cited passages and note for the exact claim. 'typology' = interpretive; faithful readers differ. Quotes are short ESV excerpts verified against esv.org.

nodes.label: Jesus Christ
nodes.summary: In the Reformed reading used here, the Bible's story moves toward Jesus. Matthew calls him the son of David and the son of Abraham.

nodes.label: The Birth of Jesus

quote.text: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

nodes.summary: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, King David's town. An angel called him Savior and Christ the Lord. Christ is the Greek title for Messiah. Both mean Anointed One. Here the title names the promised king.

nodes.label: The First Gospel Promise

quote.text: he shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

nodes.summary: In the Reformed reading used here, Genesis 3:15 is the first promise of Christ. The woman's offspring will crush the serpent, though he is wounded.

nodes.label: Abraham's Offspring

quote.text: in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed

nodes.summary: God told Abraham that all nations would be blessed in his offspring. Paul identifies the offspring with Christ in Galatians 3:16.

nodes.label: The Scepter of Judah
nodes.summary: Jacob said the scepter and ruler's staff would not depart from Judah until tribute came to its ruler. The New Testament identifies Jesus with Judah's tribe.

nodes.label: The Root of Jesse
nodes.summary: Isaiah said a new king would grow from Jesse's family, like a green shoot from an old stump. Jesse was King David's father.

nodes.label: Covenant with David
nodes.summary: God covenanted to establish David's house and promised that his son's kingdom would last forever.

nodes.label: Isaiah the Prophet
nodes.summary: Isaiah was a prophet in Judah. Three stops on this map are words from his book: the sign of Immanuel, the child born for us, and the shoot from Jesse's stump.

nodes.label: The Virgin's Son, Immanuel

quote.text: Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

nodes.summary: Isaiah said a virgin would have a son named Immanuel. The name means God with us.

nodes.label: Unto Us a Child Is Born

quote.text: For to us a child is born, to us a son is given

nodes.summary: Isaiah said a child would be born for us, and the government would rest on his shoulder.

nodes.label: Ruler from Bethlehem

quote.text: But you, O Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are too little to be among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel

nodes.summary: Micah said a ruler in Israel would come from Bethlehem, a town too little to be counted among the clans of Judah.

nodes.label: Bethlehem
nodes.summary: Bethlehem was David's hometown. Its Hebrew name is commonly translated house of bread. It was the town named by Micah as the source of Israel's coming ruler.

nodes.label: Mary
nodes.summary: Mary trusted God's message and became the mother of Jesus.

nodes.label: Joseph
nodes.summary: An angel called Joseph son of David. He would raise Jesus, but he was not the biological father.

nodes.label: Gabriel's Announcement

quote.text: the Lord God will give to him the throne of his father David

nodes.summary: The angel Gabriel told Mary that her son would receive the throne of his father David.

nodes.label: The Magi Seek the King
nodes.summary: Wise men from the east came looking for the child born king of the Jews, and they worshiped him.

nodes.label: I Am the Bread of Life
nodes.summary: Jesus said he is the bread of life. In John 6:35, coming to him and believing in him stand alongside no hunger and no thirst.

edges.note: Paul says God's Son was born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). That statement is explicit. Identifying this birth as the fulfillment of Genesis 3:15 is the confessional Reformed reading, not a direct quotation or stated fulfillment in Galatians.
The promise gets more specific. It will come through Abraham's family. Many Reformed readers see it this way. Genesis itself does not say these two verses are the same promise.
Paul says the promises to Abraham and his offspring point to Christ. Matthew calls Jesus the son of Abraham. Christ and Messiah both mean Anointed One.
The New Testament calls Jesus the Lion from Judah's tribe, and says he came from Judah's family.
Paul quotes Isaiah 11:10 and says it is about Jesus.

Matthew traces David's line to Joseph, calls him Mary's husband, and records that Joseph named Jesus. Christian interpreters commonly describe Joseph as Jesus' legal father, but Matthew does not use that legal phrase. Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit.

The sign of Immanuel is Isaiah 7:14, in Isaiah's own book. Matthew 1:22-23 quotes it and says it took place to fulfill what the Lord had spoken by the prophet. Matthew does not name Isaiah in that verse. He names him elsewhere, as at Matthew 3:3 and Matthew 4:14.
This stop is Isaiah 9:1-7, in Isaiah's own book. Matthew 4:14-16 names Isaiah and quotes the opening of it, Isaiah 9:1-2, about the light in Galilee. Matthew does not quote the child in Isaiah 9:6-7.
The shoot from Jesse's stump is Isaiah 11:1. Paul quotes Isaiah 11:10 at Romans 15:12 and names Isaiah as the one who says it.
Matthew quotes Isaiah 9:1-2 about Jesus teaching in Galilee. He does not quote Isaiah 9:6-7 there. Christians read the child and Davidic throne in Isaiah 9:6-7 with Gabriel's promise in Luke 1:32-33.
When Herod asked where the king would be born, the priests read him Micah 5:2.
They asked where the child was who had been born king of the Jews.
